caption_hook: Arkansas has a diamond-bearing volcano, giant quartz crystals and the first national river.

layers.name: PRAIRIE CREEK PIPE
layers.what: A volcano blasted up from deep underground, carrying diamonds with it. Its rock, called lamproite, cooled in the vent, and erosion has since exposed it near Murfreesboro.
layers.bonus: Visitors keep what they find. The 40-carat Uncle Sam is the largest diamond found in the U.S.

layers.name: HARTSHORNE SANDSTONE
layers.hook: Sand from a vanished river system
layers.what: River sands piled up thickly in a basin south of the old Ozarks and hardened into a tough sandstone. It caps the flat-topped mountains of the Arkansas River Valley.
layers.bonus: Petit Jean Mountain, topped by this sandstone, hosts Arkansas's first state park.

layers.name: BOONE FORMATION
layers.what: A warm shallow sea left layers of limestone with bands of hard chert. Rivers like the Buffalo have carved it into tall bluffs and caves across the Ozarks.
layers.bonus: The Buffalo became the first National River in the U.S. in 1972.

layers.name: ARKANSAS NOVACULITE
layers.what: A very fine-grained, glassy rock made mostly of microscopic quartz. It is hard and evenly gritty, so it has been used for centuries as a sharpening stone.
layers.bonus: Native Americans quarried it for tools long before Hot Springs became a spa town.

layers.name: CRYSTAL MTN SANDSTONE
layers.what: Ouachita Mountain rocks were folded and squeezed when continents collided. Hot, silica-rich water seeped into cracks in them and slowly grew clear quartz crystals.
layers.bonus: Mount Ida calls itself the Quartz Crystal Capital of the World.
